title: U.S. House · Massachusetts's 8th District
area: South Boston, Quincy and southern suburbs of Boston, including Braintree, Weymouth and parts of Middlesex County.

context.text: Incumbent Stephen Lynch defeated Patrick Roath 56.9%-43.1% in the September 1, 2026 Democratic primary. Robert Burke won the Republican primary unopposed (99.0% of the vote, having previously run against Lynch in 2022 and 2024). Rasheed Walters is running as an unenrolled (independent) candidate.

summary.text: Stephen Lynch is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Representative for Massachusetts's 8th District. A South Boston native and former ironworker who led his union local, he sits on the House Financial Services and Oversight and Government Reform committees.

background.text: Born and raised in South Boston; graduated South Boston High School and began his career as an ironworker, becoming his union local's youngest president at age 30.
Later earned a B.A. from Wentworth Institute of Technology (1988), a J.D. from Boston College (1991), and a master's in public administration from Harvard's Kennedy School (1999).

priorities.text: Increase patient access to health care, rein in premiums and drug prices, and build on the Affordable Care Act to cover more Americans.
Support commonsense gun-violence prevention measures, including universal background checks.
Support strong labor unions, a higher minimum wage, and worker protections.

positions.summary: States he is opposed to efforts to curtail reproductive rights and has voted against legislation to defund Planned Parenthood.
positions.quote: He is also strongly opposed to misguided efforts to curtail reproductive rights and has fought on the House Floor against legislation designed to defund organizations such as Planned Parenthood that provide critical family planning and women's healthcare services.

positions.summary: Describes himself as a proponent of gun-control legislation and cites House Democrats' work to require universal background checks for gun purchases.
positions.quote: Democrats in the House have worked hard to address these issues: most notably passing bills to require universal background checks for gun purchases, closing a loophole for buyers at gun shows and online, and extending the initial F.B.I. background check review period from three days to ten.

positions.summary: Says he is committed to protecting the Affordable Care Act and building on it so that more Americans are covered, including expanding eligibility for federal financial assistance and Medicaid.
positions.quote: The Congressman is committed to protecting the Affordable Care Act (ACA) and building upon it to reform and improve it in order to ensure that more Americans are covered.

positions.summary: Says America needs a long-term plan including alternatives to fossil fuels, describes an "all of the above" energy policy, and has cosponsored climate legislation.
positions.quote: Congressman Lynch believes America needs to have a long-term plan for reducing dependence on foreign oil, pursuing alternatives to fossil fuels, and improving efficiency across the entire energy spectrum.

record.text: Assigned to the House Committee on Financial Services and the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, including the Delivering on Government Efficiency Subcommittee and the Military and Foreign Affairs Subcommittee, in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).
Served as Ranking Member of the Financial Services Subcommittee on Digital Assets, Financial Technology and Inclusion in the 118th Congress (2023-2024).

candidates.name: Robert Burke
candidates.ballotNote: Won the September 1, 2026 Republican primary unopposed (99.0% of the vote); previously the Republican nominee against Lynch in 2022 and 2024.

summary.text: Robert Burke is the Republican nominee for Massachusetts's 8th District, running against incumbent Stephen Lynch for a third time. A Boston-born videographer, his campaign website lists positions on voter ID, immigration, jobs, public safety, healthcare and the criminal-justice system.

background.text: Born in Boston, Massachusetts; career experience includes starting a videography service.
Previously the Republican nominee for this seat in 2022 and 2024, losing to Lynch both times.

priorities.text: Voter integrity: supports requiring U.S. citizenship and voter ID, and says he supports the SAVE Act.
Immigration: says he supports a complete pause on immigration programs, including H-1B visas and Temporary Protected Status, pending review.
Jobs and affordability: says he would prioritize cutting taxes, bringing back manufacturing, and reducing inflation.

positions.summary: Campaign priorities page calls for passing the SAVE America Act and says voters must be U.S. citizens.

statements.quote: How can anybody feel safe when crime is up, cops are being defunded, and the streets feel lawless?!
Boxer Works pushes personal catastrophic insurance you buy yourself, with benefits for staying fit and eating right.

candidates.researchNotes: Campaign priorities page read in full. His statement on the immigration pause and tax cuts do not address the guide statements on deportations or taxing high earners, so they are listed only under priorities.

candidates.name: Rasheed Walters

summary.text: Rasheed Walters is running as an unenrolled (independent) candidate for Massachusetts's 8th District. His campaign website has policy pages on trade, immigration, healthcare, affordability and zoning.

priorities.text: Housing and energy affordability: says he would fight for affordable energy and housing, including limits on visa programs and legislation on federal building mandates and institutional purchases of single-family homes.
Immigration: says he would end work and student visa programs and support removal of non-citizens convicted of certain crimes.
Trade and manufacturing: says he would reject free trade deals and enforce tariffs to restore American manufacturing.
Corruption: says he would request a federal audit of pandemic and relief funding spent in Massachusetts.

positions.summary: Campaign site says he would push for federal funding to increase deportation capacity and for removal proceedings after state convictions of people who are in the U.S. illegally.
positions.quote: I will push for federal funding to increase deportation capacity and work with district attorneys to ensure state convictions trigger immediate federal removal proceedings.

positions.summary: Campaign site says he would write Section 301 and Section 232 tariffs into permanent law and impose additional tariffs on foreign semiconductors, automobiles and auto parts.
positions.quote: I will impose 40 to 50 percent tariffs on foreign automobiles and 35 percent tariffs on auto parts

positions.summary: Campaign site says he would raise corporate taxes on multinational companies that offshore production.
positions.quote: I will raise corporate taxes on multinational companies that offshore production.

positions.summary: Campaign site opposes the MBTA Communities Act, a state law requiring zoning for multifamily housing, and says he would defend local zoning control.
positions.quote: I will defend suburban communities' constitutional right to local zoning control.

positions.summary: Campaign site rejects universal or single-payer health care and proposes an optional government-subsidized plan at $75 per month alongside private insurance.
positions.quote: Universal healthcare sounds good until you examine who profits.

statements.quote: If they want taxpayer dollars, they pay workers $25 per hour minimum with full benefits, or they lose federal business.
statements.context: On his campaign site's trade page, about companies with federal contracts or tax benefits

statements.quote: I will work with the Departments of Energy and Interior to accelerate pipeline and energy infrastructure projects.
statements.context: On his campaign site's affordability page

candidates.researchNotes: Independent. Ballotpedia lists no Candidate Connection survey. Statements and positions come from the policy pages of his campaign site; no news coverage or debate was reviewed. His site also has pages on potholes, bike lanes, drugs and crime and the COVID response, which are not on the guide issue list.
